items.headline: Stocks try to recoup losses after Thursday's rout; tech still on edge
items.note: CNBC says stocks recouped some of Thursday's losses, when the Nasdaq fell 5.5% into a correction (worst day since April 2025) and the Dow fell about 1,800 points. I couldn't confirm Friday's closing index numbers. The VIX was around 24, and strategists warn it could take another week to bottom.

items.headline: October payrolls rise 165,000, nearly triple forecasts; unemployment 4.1%
items.note: Strong hiring keeps Fed hike talk alive, but about 2 million people (27.6% of the jobless) have been out of work 27+ weeks, the highest share since late 2021. A tougher market for job seekers, even when headline numbers look good.

items.headline: Fed's Daly: 'we're going to have to tighten policy further'
items.note: She says households are on a 'treadmill of high inflation.' Wages rose 3.1% in October versus 3.7% September inflation, so real pay is falling. The Fed's target range is 3.75%-4%.

items.headline: Next week: October CPI on Tuesday
items.note: Early estimates call for 3.9% inflation year over year, versus 3.7% previously. A hot number would raise hike odds and pressure tech stocks again.

items.headline: Democratic sweep clouds the outlook for US data-center buildout
items.note: Investors worry about moratoriums or tighter data-center rules in some states, part of the AI sell-off (Magnificent 7 lost about $1 trillion Thursday). Dan Ives calls it a buying opportunity and expects most permitted projects to get built. Opinions differ.

items.headline: ING reportedly seeks buyers for about $500M of data-center loans
items.note: Banks are moving AI data-center credit risk to private credit and insurers, including loans tied to the Stargate project. Bids are due Nov. 19. It's a sign of rising AI-debt worries.

items.headline: Microsoft reportedly winding down Oracle deal to rent AI cloud capacity
items.note: CNBC reported the news on Friday but its page gave no details on size or reasons. Watch for confirmation, since it bears on AI capacity demand.

items.headline: Oil falls under $100 Brent midweek, then choppy
items.note: ICE Brent fell 8.7% Wednesday to under $100 for the first time since September. The Bank of England raised rates by 25 basis points Thursday.

items.headline: Nvidia earnings come later this month
items.note: CNBC notes Nvidia reports outside next week's calendar. After losing about $440 billion in value Thursday, that report is the next big test for AI chip sentiment.

learn.explain: Real wages are your pay after adjusting for inflation, which tells you what your paycheck can actually buy. If wages grow 3.1% but prices grow 3.7%, as in today's data, real wages fall about 0.6 points, so people are effectively poorer even with raises. That is why the Fed worries about inflation and why a 'strong' pay number isn't always good news.
